title: Uniform vanishing of the higher direct images
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $q=p^a$ and
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime
$\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer
$\varpi_E$ of its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$.
Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$, the finite local
coefficient ring of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be
finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite-type morphism
[def-weil-finite-type-morphism] which is separated (its diagonal is a
closed immersion, as in [def-weil-proper-morphism]).

For an integer $N\geq0$, define $\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;N)$ to be the predicate
$$
 \text{for every sheaf }M\text{ of }A\text{-modules on }X_{\Et}
 \text{ and every integer }r>N,\qquad R^rf_*M=0.
$$
Here $X_{\Et}$ and $Y_{\Et}$ are the small étale sites
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the module coefficients are the constant ring
sheaves, and $R^rf_*M=\mathcal H^r(Rf_*(M[0]))$ uses the module-sheaf
version of the derived direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; zero
means the zero sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$. The bound $N$ is fixed independently of
$M$. Every such $M$ is torsion as an abelian sheaf: since $A$ is finite,
some positive integer $c$ satisfies $c\cdot1_A=0$, so $cM=0$.

This is the analogue on the small étale sites, for all module sheaves, of
the vanishing clause (2) of $\mathrm{FIN}$
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness], whose sheaves are
constructible and on the small pro-étale sites. It imposes neither
constructibility of the higher direct images nor vanishing after base
change, and does not assert existence of any bound.

Its body is definitionally exactly the node's all-module-sheaf vanishing condition, with integer degrees q > N and IsZero on the target sheaf.
